detail: p. 2226, recommendation 1. All seven maternal indications and their individual I/A, I/B or I/C grades match, including the exposure timing.

p. 2226, recommendation 2. The familial indication is congenital heart disease (CHD), both for the first-degree relative and for the Mendelian association. Generic heart disease broadens referral. The remaining indications, both NT cutoffs, the ductus venosus condition and the individual grades match.
p. 2226, recommendation 3. The four IIa indications and the B/B/A/A evidence grades match. The NT condition is above the 95th centile (at least 3.0 mm).

p. 2226, recommendation 4. The second-degree relative must have congenital heart disease. Generic heart disease expands this IIb/B indication. The listed exposures, anatomical finding and other grades match.

p. 2226, recommendation 5. The family-history exception refers specifically to isolated congenital heart disease. The HbA1c cutoff and all III grades match. The vitamin K caveat accurately flags an internal inconsistency: recommendation 5 prints “agonists”, whereas Table 2 lists antagonists. Refer the discrepancy to the editor.
p. 2226, recommendation 6. The cine and still acquisition, sweep direction and standard views are graded I/A. Short- and long-axis views carry I/B.
p. 2226, recommendation 7. The structures, side-to-side size comparisons, relative arterial positions and 2D cine and still-image requirements agree (I/A).
p. 2226, recommendation 8. The colour targets carry I/B and the pulsed valve and ductus venosus assessments I/B/C. The systemic venous targets explicitly include both venae cavae.
p. 2226, recommendation 9. All three rhythm techniques and the qualitative function assessment, including assessment for cardiomegaly and hydrops, match (I/B).
p. 2226, recommendation 10. The additional measurements apply in specific clinical situations (I/B/C). The isovolumic times cover both contraction and relaxation.
p. 2226, recommendation 11. The bilateral valve and ventricular length comparisons and the six venous, arch and umbilical Doppler targets agree (IIa/B).
p. 2227, recommendation 12. The two pulsed Doppler targets are conditional on the clinical situation (IIb/B/C).

p. 2227, recommendation 13. The fetal magnetocardiography indication includes known as well as suspected conduction system abnormalities. The ledger gives only suspected disease. The research status, other indications and IIa/B/C grade match.

p. 2227, recommendation 14. The I/A recommendation applies to fetuses with known congenital heart disease. The ledger expands this to known heart disease generally. The counselling, testing offer and detailed survey match.

p. 2227, recommendation 15. The brain MRI indication concerns a suspected brain abnormality in known congenital heart disease. The ledger omits congenital. The separate lung-volume indication in diaphragmatic hernia and IIa/B grade agree.

p. 2227, recommendation 16. The brain MRI screening population is known congenital heart disease. The ledger broadens it to all known heart disease. For suspected pulmonary hypoplasia the chest/lung MRI is specifically to assess lung volumes (IIb/B).

p. 2227, recommendation 17. The statement limits this IIb/C recommendation to known congenital heart disease. The timing and hypoxaemia/acidosis risk conditions on nonstress testing and biophysical profiling are otherwise preserved.

p. 2227, recommendation 18. The sustained rhythm, mean rate greater than 200 bpm, proximity to term and arrhythmia-related hydrops conditions match (I/A). For terminological consistency the statement uses “persistent” for PJRT.

p. 2227, recommendation 19. For AV block the IIa/B recommendation is to consider sympathomimetics. At higher ventricular rates its structural criterion is severe congenital heart disease, not severe heart disease of any cause. The less-than-55 bpm cutoff and heart failure or hydrops alternatives match.

p. 2227, recommendation 20. The statement regards consideration of medical therapy as reasonable. The ledger applies “reasonable” directly to therapy. Preserve the consideration language. Intermittent VT, the strict greater-than-200 bpm threshold and IIa/B are correct.
p. 2227, recommendation 21. The dexamethasone conditions have grade IIb/B and the separate digoxin consideration for signs of heart failure IIb/A.

p. 2227, recommendation 22. The two absence-of-benefit groups have III/A and III/B/C respectively. For clarity apply the absence of compromise or hydrops to both intermittent SVT and intermittent VT, with the less-than-200 bpm condition confined to VT.

p. 2227, recommendation 23. The fourth IIb/B/C indication specifies pulmonary atresia with an intact ventricular septum (PA/IVS). The ledger leaves the septum unspecified in a list also discussing the atrial septum. The three other lesion combinations match.
p. 2227, recommendation 24. The d-TGA indication is independent of the sustained or uncontrolled tachyarrhythmia indication, which requires heart failure or hydrops (I/B/C).

p. 2227, recommendation 25. The pulmonary venous forward/reversed ratio is strictly below 3. The alternative hyperoxia test is in the third trimester. The complete heart block criteria and IIa/B/C grade match.
p. 2227, recommendation 26. The absent pulmonary valve tetralogy indication and the Ebstein anomaly with hydrops indication match (IIb/C).
p. 2227, recommendation 27. The shunt, most ductal-dependent, and controlled rhythm groups match the III/B/C recommendation about specialised delivery room care.
